Reject candidates whose trajectory is not positive

Source: R/screening.R
screen_positive.Rd

A sum of exponentials with mixed signs is not constrained to be positive, so a candidate can dip below zero between observations. The likelihood sees only the observation times, so such an excursion costs nothing there and the candidate survives into the fitted population, where it appears in posterior summaries as a dive to the floor and back.

Usage

screen_positive(
  candidates,
  trajectory,
  grid = seq(0, 60, by = 1),
  floor = 0.01
)

Arguments

candidates

A data frame of candidate parameter values.

trajectory

A function (time, theta) as in trajectory_loglik(). It must be called in a way that returns the raw solution, not one already floored at a positive value.

grid

Dense time grid on which positivity is checked.

floor

Smallest value treated as positive.

Value

A list with the logical vector keep, the screened candidates, and the rejected count.

Details

The grid must be dense enough to catch an excursion between visits; evaluating on the observation times defeats the purpose.

See also

screen_candidates()

Examples

cand <- data.frame(a = c(1, 1), b = c(0.5, 5))
f <- function(t, th) th$a - th$b * t          # the second goes negative
screen_positive(cand, f, grid = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05))$keep
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE
